summary: This Dockerfile sets up a Python development container with two stages. First, it creates a base image with Python 3.10, installs Linux and Python dependencies, and configures Python to output logs immediately. Then it builds a development image on top of that, creating a non-root user account, setting up VS Code server directories, customizing the shell prompt, and configuring bash history to persist across container restarts.

explanations.7: ARG declares a variable that can be passed when building the image (like a parameter), setting a default value of '/app' for the application directory.
explanations.17: FROM pulls the official Python image with version 3.10-slim as the starting point, and 'AS base' names this stage so we can reference it later.
explanations.20: Setting this environment variable tells Python not to generate .pyc compiled files, which saves space since they're not needed in a container.
explanations.27: WORKDIR creates the specified directory inside the container and makes it the current working directory for all subsequent commands.
explanations.30: The --mount flags are optimizations: the cache mount reuses downloaded packages across builds (faster rebuilds), and 'set -e -x' makes the script exit on errors and print each command.
explanations.45: This runs pip install while mounting the requirements.txt from your host machine without copying it, and caches pip downloads so future builds are faster.
explanations.56: This creates a new image stage called 'development' that starts from our 'base' stage, so it inherits everything we already installed.
explanations.76: addgroup creates a user group with the specified GID (group ID number), which is used to organize file permissions.
explanations.78: adduser creates the actual user account with various flags: --system makes it a system user, --disabled-password means no login password needed, --gecos '' skips extra user info.
explanations.92: This appends a custom command to .bashrc (shell startup file) that sets up a fancy shell prompt displaying the container name, 'DEV' status, and current user.
explanations.98: This creates a snippet of bash commands that saves command history to a file instead of just memory, so history persists even after the container stops.
